verdictBasis: Every attack axis in the dispatch fails on all three entries, and the decision merits of all three pass. The single SHOULD-FIX is in the shared header, which governs all three entries, so each inherits it and none can take CONSENT under the dispatch's own rule. If the header line is corrected, all three are consentable on this reviewer's analysis with no further change.

shouldFixRecorded.scope: file-level; inherited by D-051, D-052 and D-053 equally
shouldFixRecorded.location: header, line 3 — '> **Status:** DRAFT — not yet dispatched.'
shouldFixRecorded.finding: The subject asserts it has not been dispatched. It has: it is the frozen subject of this turn-1 adversarial review, held at chmod 0444, and this verdict is the review of record for it. The statement is false at the moment it is being read.
shouldFixRecorded.whyThisGrade: I considered a NOTE and rejected it. The three sibling drafts I reviewed in this same family — D-060, D-061 and D-065 — all carry 'DRAFT — under review', so the correct form exists and is in active use; this is a departure, not a convention. More decisively, D-059 turn 3 turned on exactly this class of defect: the subject misdescribed its own protocol state, I graded it a NOTE, the other reviewer graded it higher, the cycle went CONTESTED, and the register recorded 'Decision merits passed on both sides. Process freeze failed.' I recorded a self-correction in my D-064 verdict accepting that the harder grading produced the root-cause fix. Grading this a NOTE would repeat the error I already committed to not repeating.
shouldFixRecorded.whyNotMustFix: It touches no decision content, and the whole status line is replaced at adoption — every adopted entry I sampled (D-028, D-029, D-030, D-047, D-048, D-060, D-065) carries '**ADOPTED <date>.**' plus reviewer verdicts, so the false clause never reaches the register.
shouldFixRecorded.fix: One line: 'DRAFT — under review.' No other change is required by this reviewer's analysis.

notesRecorded.whyItIsNotAFinding: Three independent reasons. First, the label says 'at authoring', which is a claim about when the value was measured, not about current state, and that claim is true. Second, a COORD pin inside an entry that will itself be appended to COORD is stale by construction, so self-staleness is structural rather than a defect. Third, and decisively, I did not rely on the label — I re-verified every register-dependent claim in the preamble against live bytes, and all of them hold. The staleness is explained by this being an older draft, numbered below D-058/D-060/D-061/D-064/D-065, dispatched after those cycles moved COORD several times.
notesRecorded.onTheMissingRemeasurementClause: I checked the right comparison class rather than the recent one. The adopted selection entries this draft names as its form — D-028, D-029, D-030, D-047, D-048 — carry no measured-inputs table and no remeasurement clause at all. The table here is extra rigor beyond the selection form, not a required pin table with a broken contract. The remeasurement clause I saw in D-060, D-061 and D-065 belongs to the D-057 owner-recording form, which is a different instrument.

summary: Subject and prompt both held at their dispatched digests, subject read-only at both ends. Every attack axis fails, including the two I expected to be live. The 'hides D-002 rides' axis fails completely: D-002 enumerates exactly five rides, and all five are disclosed and correctly partitioned — four to D-051 (SARIF/RunId+fingerprint, cache-index keys, Coverage/subjectScopeCommitment, PlanId/typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot) and one to D-052 (doctor D9 mapping DR-114 plus containment goldens DR-G21). D-053 carries no rides clause, and that is correct rather than an omission: D-002 names no DR-009 rides at all, which I confirmed by direct search. The 'unseverable bundle' axis fails: each entry names one row, excludes the other seven by name, and carries its own decision, alternatives, readiness effect, reversibility and overturn code. D-053's DR-204 claim, which is the one assertion in the draft that could have been false, is verified true at source — the adjudication rules 'UTC-BOUNDARY ARTIFACT, NOT A DEFECT; DR-009/R09 RELIANCE CLEAN ON THE DATE QUESTION' and records the D-001 gate as DISCHARGED. My objection is not about any of that. It is one false sentence in the shared header: the file says it has not been dispatched while under review.
whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 080a3c203134787195e76ed73e5c14515282ee9e3dd6afaae4fa4d80ff2a4aa5, three measurements at start and again at end, equal to the dispatched frozen digest, -r--r--r-- at both ends. Prompt held at 9484351c428e8515085ad274238f03decf707830fcd254f94dbd532783f03899.

The attack 'hides D-002 rides' fails, tested by extracting D-002's own enumeration rather than by matching the dispatch's list. D-002's identity-dependencies section names five rides: SARIF for analyze riding DR-006's RunId derivation recipe and Finding fingerprint; the rebuildable cache/index state class riding the parked cache/regeneration-key recipes (DR-006); Coverage on the TypeScript provider dispatch path riding the parked subjectScopeCommitment (DR-006); PlanId for the TypeScript role riding a producing rule for typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot (DR-006's park-coverage property); and doctor's D9 mapping (DR-114) with containment goldens (DR-G21) riding DR-007. D-051 clause 4 names the first four, each with the same parked identity D-002 attaches to it. D-052 clause 4 names the fifth, with the same DR-114 and DR-G21 references. All five are present and none is attached to the wrong row.

D-053 having no rides clause is correct, not an omission. I searched D-002 for DR-009, LN-13, derivationDigest, R1-PARK, one-shot and no-reuse and found zero genuine hits — the only 'R-1' match is a false positive inside the substring 'DR-123'. D-002 names no DR-009 rides, so there are none to disclose. D-053 nonetheless carries the ride-shaped consequence in clause 3: 'Identity-dependent implementation waits.'

The draft's preamble statement of the consequence is faithful to D-002 T2-04, which reads 'The SARIF consequence clause holds SYMMETRICALLY for all five rides (T2-04): if any named condition-1 closure lands by scoped disposition rather than binding recipes, the dependent feature … ships reduced, re-scoped, or waits … none of them survives on prose.' The draft's 'ships reduced, re-scoped, or waits' and D-052's 'ship reduced, re-scoped, or wait' both track it, and D-051's alternatives section cites 'D-002 T2-04 symmetry' accurately.

The attack 'unseverable bundle (D-025 defect)' fails, and I checked what the D-025 defect actually was rather than assuming. COORD records that 'D-025 has no register entry and is not CONTESTED' — an unadopted draft, superseded, whose closed three-form Route C set was rejected. The cure was the severable D-028/D-029/D-030 form, which this draft names and follows. Structurally each entry declares 'Subject: DR-00X only', excludes the other seven rows by name in clause 2, and carries its own Decision, Alternatives, Readiness effect and Reversibility sections plus a distinct overturn code C-D051 / C-D052 / C-D053. D-051, D-052 and D-053 are all unused numbers in COORD, so there is no collision.

D-053's DR-204 claim is true at source, which was the single assertion most capable of being false. The entry says 'DR-204 already ruled the dialect-repair date anomaly CLEAN for reliance; this entry does not re-open that adjudication.' dr-204.re-review-independent.json records adjudication 4-dialect-repair-review-date with ruling 'UTC-BOUNDARY ARTIFACT, NOT A DEFECT; DR-009/R09 RELIANCE CLEAN ON THE DATE QUESTION', and its relianceRuling states that the D-001 gate — quoted there as 'DR-009 route A, gated on DR-204's adjudication of the date anomaly before reliance' — 'is DISCHARGED'. The gate the earlier routing entry imposed on DR-009 is therefore lifted.

I also read the proviso the ruling attaches, since a partial recital would have been a finding: reliance is clean 'PROVIDED reliance continues to bind the reviewed instrument digests and carries the five advisories as live advisories'. D-053 selects a route, writes no disposition, marks nothing SATISFIED, and states it does not re-open the adjudication — which preserves the ruling together with its proviso rather than reciting a stripped version of it.

The attack 'invents D9 codes' fails. D-052 clause 3 states 'This entry invents no D9 code', and its alternatives section explicitly rejects 'Invent preview D9 codes for retention loss or observation→faultCause' on the ground that file 08 and D-002 both forbid it. Its claim that 'd9-exit-contract.v1.14 stays the live contract' is true: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE §3 binds D9 to d9-exit-contract.v1.14.json at 8dd33038…, the file exists on disk, and COORD's routing line reads 'DR-007 route A: D9 successor to v1.14.'

The attack 'treats applied EIR v12 or r1 v1.9 as SATISFIED of parks' fails on both rows. D-051 clause 3: 'EIR v12 is the applied lineage head (D-003). Application of a head is not binding recipes and is not SATISFIED of this row.' D-053 clause 3: 'r1 v1.9 is the applied lineage head (D-005). Application of a head is not park closure and is not SATISFIED of this row', reinforced by an alternative that rejects treating applied r1 v1.9 as SATISFIED of LN-13 / derivationDigest / R1-PARK because 'D-005 closed application of the head, not the parks'. Both citations resolve: D-003 is 'Apply evidence-identity-recipes.v12' and D-005 is 'Apply r1-lifetime-neutrality.conformance.v1.9', both ADOPTED.

The attack 'coordinator becomes recording authority' fails identically in all three entries, each carrying: 'Coordinator selects. Named owners record. Coordinator may draft. D-000 does not make the coordinator [the identity-owning surfaces / the D9 authority / the R-1 authority]. Independent review is required. A coordinator-composed SATISFIED is unlawful (DR-204).' I confirmed that last clause is the standing formulation by finding the identical sentence in an adopted entry.

The attack 'writes a disposition in this entry' fails: the header states 'Does not write dispositions', and each entry's final clause states 'Writes no disposition. Marks nothing SATISFIED. Authorizes no blueprint.'

The attacks 'silent SATISFIED or condition-1 discharge' and 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' fail. Each entry states that only 'A completed, reviewed, owner-recorded disposition may discharge condition 1 … within the scope it names', keeping the discharge conditional on a future act by the named owner; each preserves 'Conditions 2–5 remain. Condition 5 remains the only implementation authorization'; and each records 'Readiness effect: Zero at adoption.'

The three owning-authority recitals are exact string matches against file 08's owner cells: DR-006 'Each identity-owning V1 surface + FACT-PLANE/evidence authorities + coordinator'; DR-007 'D9 authority + evidence/retention owner'; DR-009 'R-1/evidence authorities'.

The preamble's completeness claim holds against live COORD, not merely the stale pin. It says these three are the remaining inherited V1 prerequisites with no Route B selection. Sweeping COORD for adopted selection entries returns exactly five — D-028 (DR-005), D-029 (DR-008 integration half), D-030 (DR-003 scoped preview TM), D-047 (DR-002), D-048 (DR-004) — matching the claimed set DR-002/003/004/005/008. With DR-001 SATISFIED, DR-010 on Route C jointly with DR-117 (confirmed by COORD's routing line 'DR-010 route C PREFERENCE-LADEN (P-1/P-2/G3 successor, jointly with DR-117 and R16)') and DR-011's residuals routed by their owning surfaces, the remainder of DR-001..011 is exactly DR-006, DR-007 and DR-009.
The attack 'file 08 edited' fails: file 08 measures unchanged at its cited digest 6547e6ac… and git reports zero modified tracked files. I wrote one file and edited and committed nothing.

Reversibility is stated identically and correctly in all three: 'Total before any dependent disposition lands. After one lands, overturn also requires that disposition's owning-authority supersession', with the per-entry overturn code.

objectNote: I OBJECT on all three entries with zero MUST-FIX and one SHOULD-FIX, and I want the shape of that recorded precisely: the decision merits of D-051, D-052 and D-053 all pass. Every axis the dispatch named fails, including the two that had real teeth — the five D-002 rides are all disclosed and correctly partitioned, and D-053's DR-204 reliance claim is true at source with the gate recorded DISCHARGED. The objection is one sentence in the shared header claiming the file has not been dispatched while it sits frozen at 0444 under turn-1 review. I considered grading it a NOTE and did not, because that is the same call I made on D-059's turn-3 self-misdescription, it went CONTESTED, and I have already recorded a self-correction accepting that the harder grading was right. Correct the line and, on my analysis, all three entries are consentable unchanged.
